🇲🇽✊ "They criticize us because we say that all students deserve a scholarship. All of them." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Ocozocoautla, Chiapas As head of government of Mexico City she found a "talented children" scholarship only for students with 9 and 10 averages. A study showed it did not push the others to get better grades. Instead it split the classroom between the "supposed good student" and the "supposed bad student." After giving scholarships to every primary and secondary student, all of them got better grades, learned more and dropped out less. Chiapas now covers every student from primary through university: 1,219,971 students, an investment of over 9.2 billion pesos. She also announced a medical and nursing school for the Universidad Nacional Rosario Castellanos campus in Comitán.
banner: WHY EVERY STUDENT GETS A SCHOLARSHIP

text: 🇲🇽✊ "Father Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla said no to castes, no to slavery. Benito Juárez García said we are all equal before the law. Nobody is more than anyone else." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Chiapa de Corzo, Chiapas Closing the National Day for Peace at CONALEP 22 in Chiapa de Corzo, she said the goal of talking about emotions in school is to keep young people away from drugs and alcohol, "which is also a drug," to build peace and friendship, and above all to recognize "that we are all great people, that nobody is less than anyone else." During the colony, she noted, there were castes, "those who were worth more and those who were worth less." "Each one of us is a different person, but we have the right to the same."

🇲🇽✊ "It is very machista that women have to hide our age. Women can be whatever we want to be, and we age with dignity, just like men." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Ocozocoautla, Chiapas "This year I turned 64," she told the students in Ocozocoautla, recalling that she grew up in a time when women were told never to say their age, "as if growing old were something bad." She then told them how she studied at the UNAM's CCH Sur high school, studied physics, then did a master's and a doctorate in engineering, including time abroad: "I could not have done that if the UNAM had not given me a scholarship to study."
